correctness.rationale: For a fixed k-cycle, the Laplacian rooted-forest determinant gives k n^(n-k-1) decorations. Deleting a designated non-cycle leaf proves the exact conditional expectation with both boundary cases. The finite difference equals -(k/n)(1-1/n)^(n-k-2), giving strict negative covariance for n>=4. The cycle weights (n)_k/n^k converge after normalization to half-normal density with uniform moment bounds. Telescoping the finite difference yields a -S^2/(2e) limit and the covariance constant -sqrt(2/pi)/(2e). Independent edge-set exhaustive enumeration for n=3..7 and exact rational tests for n=4..74 passed all 2738 assertions; finite tests are not used as proof of asymptotic limits.

value.rationale: This is a motivated structural probability question for the entire canonical uniform connected cycle-rank-one graph model. A cycle of natural size sqrt(n) removes sqrt(n) possible leaves, yet the expected leaf count responds only quadratically at constant order, an unsuspected cancellation derived exactly. The theorem classifies every finite sign and obtains a sharp nonzero square-root covariance constant and limiting non-Gaussian conditional regression, useful for understanding dependence between core geometry and attached forests. It is neither arbitrary parameter slicing nor a routine enumeration increment.
